## ⛔ Do not dispatch this card until its scope decision is made — the instance set is larger than it looks

From the `domain:devx` seat (#6023). ⚠️ This card is **not** blocked on #8886 alone, which is what this seat previously assumed and recorded. Correcting that here so it does not get acted on.

### What I got wrong

This seat held this card back behind #8886 / PR #8912 with the reasoning: *"the gate must not land before the stale page it would go red on."* The reasoning is right. **The instance set was wrong** — I treated v16 as the only stale page because it was the only one anyone had noticed.

### Measured on `origin/main` @ `85f5e78`, 2026-08-15T16:29Z

| page | says | last tag |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `v9.mdx:6` | published at **9.0.0** | `9.11.0` ❌ |
| `v12.mdx:6` | published at **12.0.0** | `12.6.0` ❌ |
| `v13.mdx:6` | published at 13.0.0 | `13.0.0` ✅ |
| `v14.mdx:6` | *current:* **14.5.0** | `14.8.0` ❌ (and `index.mdx` already says `final release: 14.8.0` — page and index disagree) |
| `v15.mdx` | no status line | `15.1.1` ➖ |

⇒ **Merging #8912 will not make `main` safe for this gate.** Landed as a naive all-majors check, it goes red on **v14, v12 and v9** on day one. A red `main` is shared damage every lane pays for, so this has to be decided *before* implementation, not discovered by CI.

### The three options, and the trap

Filed in full as **#8916**, summarised:

- **A** — scope the gate to the current / most-recent series, stating in its own failure text why older pages are out of scope.
- **B** — make #8916 a hard prerequisite: fix v9/v12/v14 first, then land an all-majors gate.
- **C** — land with an enumerated shrink-only baseline for the three known-stale pages.

⚠️ **C is the one most likely to be reached for and least likely to be right by default.** A brand-new gate whose baseline starts with three entries ships pre-compromised, and this repo's own experience is that a gate baselined at birth gets baselined again. It is defensible **only** if someone states positively why those three pages should stay stale.

### Dispatch conditions for whoever takes this

1. ⛔ Do not implement before picking A, B or C **deliberately**, and record which in the PR body with the reason.
2. ⚠️ The gate's own text must say what it is scoped to — an intentional limitation documented only inside the implementation is indistinguishable from a bug to everyone who does not read the implementation. (Same principle the grading on #8698 made mandatory.)
3. Prove it by **ablation**, not by a green run: point it at a deliberately stale fixture page and confirm it goes red for the right reason. A gate for "nothing fails when X" that has never been seen failing is the exact shape this repo keeps rediscovering.

⛔ Still not dispatched from this seat. Card stays `pm:queue`, unassigned, labels untouched.

## ✅ Scope decision made — by the maintainer, and it is none of A/B/C exactly

**Maintainer, 2026-08-15, verbatim, untranslated:**

> v14 之前的版本都不用管

This is what the card was held for. It resolves the scope question with a **principled cutoff** rather than either extreme I offered.

### The settled scope

**The gate covers `v14` and later.** Pages for majors before v14 are explicitly out of scope — their staleness is an **accepted state**, ⛔ not a baselined defect.

⚠️ That distinction is the whole reason this is better than the options I put up:

- It is **not option A** (current series only). A would have left `v14.mdx` claiming `current: 14.5.0` while `index.mdx` says `final release: 14.8.0` — the site contradicting itself on one screen.
- It is **not option C** (land with a three-entry baseline). ⛔ Nothing is baselined. A brand-new gate does not ship pre-compromised, and no "known wrong" is recorded for a future agent to learn from.
- It is a **bounded B**: exactly **one** page needs fixing first (`v14.mdx`), not three.

### ⛔ Dispatch conditions — now concrete

1. **Scope the gate to `v14`+.** ⚠️ **State the cutoff in the gate's own failure text**, with the reason. An intentional limitation documented only inside the implementation is indistinguishable from a bug to everyone who does not read the implementation — the principle the #8698 grading made mandatory, and it applies with full force to a gate that deliberately ignores four pages.
2. **Sequencing, load-bearing**: **#8916's v14 fix lands FIRST.** The gate would go red on `v14.mdx` the day it lands otherwise, and a red `main` is shared damage every lane pays for. ⚠️ The v14 fix is `content/docs/releases/` — **release-owned**, so it is a **separate docs-only PR**, ⛔ never folded into this gate's PR.
3. **Prove it by ablation, ⛔ not by a green run.** Point it at a deliberately stale fixture page and confirm it goes red **for the right reason**. A gate for *"nothing fails when a GA'd major's page still says pre-release"* that has never been seen failing is precisely the shape this repo keeps rediscovering — and it is the shape the sibling card #8678 is being fixed for right now.
4. ⚠️ Decide and state how the gate reads "what actually shipped". Tags are the authority (`git tag --list '@objectstack/spec@<major>*'`) — that is what #8912 used and what this seat verified against. ⛔ Do not derive it from the page's own prose, which is the thing under test.

### Boundary caveat, so it does not get lost

I read 「v14 之前」 as **v13 and earlier**, i.e. **v14 is in scope**. Recorded on #8916 with the reasoning and flagged as a one-word correction if the intent was "v14 and earlier" — in which case the cutoff here moves to v15 and #8916 closes with no work. ⛔ Do not implement the cutoff from this comment alone if #8916 has since been corrected; read it first.

Card stays `pm:queue`, unassigned. **Dispatchable once #8916's v14 fix has merged.**

⇒ **The gate covers `v16` and later. v15 and earlier are out of scope entirely.** ⛔ My earlier comment on this card said "v14 and later" — that was based on the first ruling and is **wrong now**. ⛔ Do not implement from it. I am leaving it visible rather than editing, so the correction is legible.

**#8916 is closed `not planned`** as a consequence — v9/v12/v14 staleness is an **accepted state**, ⛔ not a defect and ⛔ not a baseline entry.

## ✅ The prerequisite is gone — this card is dispatchable now

Both in-scope pages are **already correct**, verified on `origin/main` just now:

| page | status line | index entry | last tag |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `v16.mdx:16` | `Release status: 16.0.0 is released.` | `(final release: 16.1.0)` | `16.1.0` ✓ |
| `v17.mdx:16` | `Release status: 17.0.0 is released.` | `(current series: 17.0.0, released 2026-08-14)` | `17.0.0` ✓ |

(v16 fixed by PR #8912, v17 by PR #8882, both merged today.) ⇒ A correctly-scoped gate is **green on today's `main`** with nothing to fix first.

## ⛔⛔ TWO MEASURED HAZARDS THAT WOULD MAKE THIS GATE WRONG ON DAY ONE

I hit both while verifying the table above. Neither is hypothetical.

### 1. `sort -V` is NOT semver-aware — it ranks a prerelease ABOVE the release

```
$ printf '%s\n' '17.0.0-rc.6' '17.0.0' | sort -V
17.0.0
17.0.0-rc.6      ← sorted LAST
```

⇒ A gate that picks "the latest tag for this major" with `sort -V | tail -1` gets **`17.0.0-rc.6`** and concludes v17 is still a prerelease — **going red on a page that is correct**, which is the precise inverse of this gate's job. In semver `17.0.0-rc.6 < 17.0.0`. **Use a real semver comparison, and pin it with a `--self-test` case containing a prerelease.**

### 2. `git tag --list` in an incomplete clone silently under-reports

My local clone lists only `rc.0, rc.1, rc.2, rc.5, rc.6` for v17 — **no `17.0.0`**, and no `rc.3`/`rc.4` either. `git ls-remote --tags origin` shows all of them **including `@objectstack/spec@17.0.0`**. The clone was incomplete, not the tag missing.

⇒ In a shallow or tag-less CI checkout, a tag-based gate concludes **v17 never went GA** and goes red on a correct page. **Guard the instrument**: either ensure tags are fetched (`fetch-depth: 0` / explicit tag fetch) **and assert it** — e.g. fail loudly if the tag set for a major is empty — or derive from a source that does not depend on checkout depth. ⛔ An empty tag list must never be read as "nothing shipped".

⚠️ Both hazards are the same family and it is the family this repo keeps paying for: **the instrument was not measuring what it appeared to measure.** I caught each only by checking against a second source. Build that check into the gate rather than trusting either reading.

## Zone 1 — Ruled. ⛔ Not re-litigable.

1. **Scope: v16+.** ⚠️ **State the cutoff in the gate's own failure text, with the reason.** A deliberate limitation documented only inside the implementation is indistinguishable from a bug to everyone who does not read the implementation — the principle the #8698 grading made mandatory, and it binds hardest on a gate that ignores five pages on purpose.
2. **⛔ Nothing is baselined.** No entry for v9/v12/v13/v14/v15. A new gate does not ship pre-compromised; out-of-scope and known-broken-but-tolerated are different states and only the first applies here.
3. **⛔ Do not touch `content/docs/releases/`.** It is release-owned; this is a code PR. Both in-scope pages are already correct, so there is nothing to fix — if you find otherwise, **report it**, do not edit.
4. **Prove it by ablation, ⛔ not by a green run.** Point it at a deliberately stale fixture page (a v16-or-later page reverted to pre-release wording) and confirm it goes red **for the right reason**, then restore byte-identically. A gate for *"nothing fails when a GA'd major still says pre-release"* that has never been seen failing is the exact shape this repo keeps rediscovering — and the sibling card #8678 is in flight for that same shape right now.

## ⚠️ Collision note — read before wiring

**PR #8945 (#8754, ACCEPTed, awaiting merge) also adds a new `scripts/` gate, a `package.json` script entry, and a `lint.yml` step.** Different script file, but **the same two shared files**. ⇒ Branch from current `main`, and if #8945 lands first, **merge `origin/main` and re-check your `lint.yml` / `package.json` hunks** before pushing. ⛔ Do not resolve a conflict by dropping its entry.

## Gates

⚠️ I could not pre-derive your set — the deliverable is a **file that does not exist yet**. Run `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs <your real changed files>` on the actual diff, run what it names, report the set. Wiring into `lint.yml` pulls the `.github` family (`check:required-contexts`, `check:workflow-status-functions`, `check:shard-attestation`, `check:node-version`). Any edit ⇒ `check:nul-bytes`. **Judge by exit status**, ⛔ not by grepping for `✗`.

`scripts/` + workflows are not published package sources ⇒ `skip-changeset`.

## ✅ ACCEPT — PR #8950

Verified against the tree, ⛔ not against the report.

| check | reading |
|:--|:--|
| changed files | **3** — `scripts/check-release-page-status.mjs` (new, +887) · `.github/workflows/lint.yml` (+12) · `package.json` (+1) |
| ⛔ `content/docs/releases/` edits | **0** ✓ — the release-owned fence held |
| scope floor | `SCOPE_FLOOR_MAJOR = 16` ✓ |
| cutoff stated in the gate | ✓ `SCOPE_NOTE` carries the **verbatim** ruling 「只负责 v16 以后的，需要的话之前的版本删除也可以的」 and is printed on **both** the failure and OK paths |
| baseline / exception list | **none** ✓ — nothing pre-compromised |

### Both hazards were closed **structurally**, which is better than what I asked for

I asked for a correct semver comparison. What landed is better: **the gate never orders versions at all.** Set membership only, so the `sort -V` trap has no surface to exist on.

⚠️ I nearly mis-flagged this. My grep for `sort -V|sort(|localeCompare|semver` returned **8 hits**, which reads as a contradiction of that claim. Looking at them: six are **comments documenting the trap**, and the other two are `[...majors].sort((a, b) => a - b)` — sorting **integer majors**, where `a - b` is exact and prereleases do not appear. **The count was not the answer; the location was.** (Third time today that a hit count nearly produced a wrong verdict.)

Hazard 2 is closed by direction rather than by care: the instrument is the in-tree CHANGELOG cross-checked against `packages/spec/package.json`, with **git tags used only in the direction that cannot be wrong** — *a tag that exists proves a release shipped; an absent tag concludes nothing.*

**And it proved that under the failure condition, not in theory.** The dev's own container reproduced the exact defect I hit: `git tag --list '@objectstack/spec@17*'` yields rc.0/1/2/5/6 with **no `17.0.0`**, while `ls-remote` shows it exists. On that clone the gate's OK line reads *"corroborated by 1 local GA tag(s)"* — degraded corroboration — **and still passes v17 correctly**. That is the guard working, observed, not asserted.

### The ablation is the strongest I have reviewed in this lane

Four legs, each against a **real historical file pulled out of git history** rather than a synthetic fixture, each restored and verified byte-identical (`sha256` + empty `git status`) before the next:

- **A** — `v17.mdx` at its pre-fix ref ⇒ RED, 6 problems, v16/index untouched.
- **B** — `v16.mdx` pre-fix ⇒ RED, 2 problems.
- **C** — `index.mdx` pre-fix with both pages correct ⇒ RED, 3 problems.
- **D** — the **whole `content/docs/releases/` directory as it stood on 2026-08-13**, when both stale pages were live and CI was green ⇒ RED, 11 problems, all confined to v16/v17/index.

⚠️ **Leg D doubles as the cutoff proof, and that is the part I would have forgotten to ask for.** At that same ref `v9.mdx` said `published at 9.0.0` (tag `9.11.0`), `v12.mdx` `12.0.0` (tag `12.6.0`), `v14.mdx` `current: 14.5.0` (tag `14.8.0`) — **all measurably stale, all correctly unreported.** So the gate is shown to catch *and* shown not to over-reach, from one measurement.

### Meta-ablation — the check I did not think to require

> a self-test that cannot fail is this defect one layer up

Two legs, both discriminating: defanging a signal ⇒ self-test red on exactly the assertions naming it; adding a naive *"any rc.N mention"* signal ⇒ self-test red on the GREEN-page assertions **and** the live run went red on the **correct** v16 page.

### The honesty I want on the record

> my first meta-ablation was a **NO-OP, not a pass** — changing the blockquote line-join separator changed nothing because the following whitespace collapse re-joins regardless, so the mutation never reached the assertion and proved nothing

⇒ It caught its own mutation not reaching the assertion, **reported it as proving nothing**, and ran two real legs instead. That is the exact discipline — a mutant must be verified to test the failure you think it tests — applied to itself, unprompted.

### The two flagged notes — both correctly left alone

1. **A duplicated attribution footer** was appended to the PR body by the platform at create time. Platform behaviour, not a second actor. ⛔ No action; ⛔ do not "clean it up" and risk touching a body another process writes.
2. **The labeler applied `dependencies`** to a PR whose only `package.json` change is a `scripts` entry. Plausibly by design (any `package.json` touch). ⛔ Correctly **not** filed and **not** removed — removing another actor's label without knowing its rule is how label churn starts. I agree with the judgement; leaving as-is.

**Next**: confirming the gate job conclusions on #8950, then ready → auto-merge → MERGED. ⚠️ It branched from `a8189aef4` before **#8945 landed**, and #8945 also edits `lint.yml` + `package.json`. The PR body carries the resolution instruction; I will re-check those two hunks before arming.
